Today, the building retains many of its original features, including an ornate tiled entrance hall, grand carved timber staircases, feature fireplaces and expansive period rooms filled with historic character.. . Set within more than 1.4 acres of grounds at Abney Park, the property is surrounded by mature landscaping and ornamental lakes, creating a tranquil setting just minutes from the centre of Cheadle Village.. . Extending to more than 21,000 sq ft, the mansion is currently home to eight commercial occupiers and benefits from more than 75 on-site parking spaces.. . Nine striking sculptures by internationally acclaimed artists Gille and Marc will bring some of the world’s most endangered animals into the heart of Manchester this autumn, as ‘A Wild Life For Wildlife’ becomes part of Spinningfields.. . Each work creates an opportunity to encounter an endangered species in an unexpected and engaging way.. . ‘A Wild Life For Wildlife’ is part of Gille and Marc’s wider Love The Last project, a social movement driven by public art to raise awareness, funds and support for endangered animals around the world. Previous installations haven taken place across the world including the World Trade Centre in New York and Kingston and Chelsea Art Trail.. . Kayleigh Sheldon, Marketing Director, said: “Bringing ‘A Wild Life For Wildlife’ to Spinningfields is a perfect opportunity for our visitors to experience these incredible sculptures in the heart of Manchester.
